Line 1a $2,000, 1b $500 -> line 2 $1,500; line 3 $3,000, line 4 $0 -> line 5 $3,000; line 2 is not more than line 5 -> 'No. Stop. Enter -0- here. Enter -0- on Form 1040 ... line 32b'.

Single, Form 1040 line 11b $600,000, line 5d $50,000. Statute section 164(b)(7) (plaw-119-21 p. 99): 2026 applicable limitation $40,400 reduced by 30 percent of the excess of MAGI over $505,000: 30% of $95,000 = $28,500; $40,400 - $28,500 = $11,900, not less than $10,000. Line 5e = smaller of $50,000 or $11,900 = $11,900. No excluded income (MAGI = AGI).

Single, line 11b $700,000, line 5d $50,000: 30% of $195,000 = $58,500 exceeds $40,400; the reduction 'shall not result in the applicable limitation amount being less than $10,000' -> $10,000; line 5e $10,000.

Married filing separately, line 11b $300,000, line 5d $30,000. Threshold halved to $252,500 (Schedule A 2026 draft line 5e; statute 'half the threshold amount'): 30% of $47,500 = $14,250; $40,400 - $14,250 = $26,150 (not below $10,000); half for a married individual filing separately = $13,075; line 5e = smaller of $30,000 or $13,075 = $13,075. Ambiguity: the order of the floor and the halving is not printed on the form; the statute applies the $10,000 floor to the applicable limitation amount and halves the amount for a separate return.

Itemizing; gambling winnings on Schedule 1 line 8b $8,000; losses $10,000. Statute section 165(d)(1) (plaw-119-21 p. 96): '(A) shall be equal to 90 percent of the amount of such losses' = $9,000 '(B) ... allowed only to the extent of the gains' = $8,000. Schedule A (2026 draft) line 17a = $8,000.
Winnings $8,000, losses $5,000: 90% of $5,000 = $4,500, under the winnings: line 17a = $4,500 (2025 rule: $5,000).

Single, born before January 2, 1962, not blind. Rev. Proc. 2025-32 section 4.14 (p. 18): basic standard deduction $16,100; additional amount $1,650 'increased to $2,050 if the individual is also unmarried'. $16,100 + $2,050 = $18,150.
Married filing jointly, both born before January 2, 1962. $32,200 + 2 x $1,650 = $35,500 (Rev. Proc. 2025-32 p. 18).

Self-only HDHP coverage on the first day of every month of 2026, under 55, not married: Line 3 Limitation Chart 'Enter $4,400 on the line below for the month' x 12 / 12 = $4,400; rp-25-19 p. 2 'is $4,400'.

Family coverage all year, unmarried, 55 or older at the end of 2026: chart 'If, at the end of 2026, you were unmarried and age 55 or older, enter $9,750 for the month' -> $9,750 (i8889 2026 draft p. 7).

Standard deduction taken (not itemizing) and $500 of cash gifts to charity on Schedule A line 11's question: Form 1040 (2026 draft) line 12f 'Charitable contribution deduction for non-itemizers (see instructions)'; the instructions are not published, so the proposal refuses (forms-proposed/f1040.yaml, f1040.gate.nonitemizer_gifts).
